newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Report says steady decline in Australian HIV/AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Report says steady decline in Australian HIV/AIDS.

text.p: A slow, steady decline in HIV and AIDS infections can be expected in Australia, according to the 1997 annual HIV/AIDS report which found an estimated 11,000 people infected with the deadly virus.

HIV/AIDS infections in Australia had been falling since 1994 due to safe sex campaigns and syringe exchange programmes for heroin users, said the Australian National Council on AIDS report released on Friday.
"Surveillance indicates that a peak in incidence was reached in 1994 and that there is potential for a continuing decline in the future," said council chairman Chris Puplick.

However, the report warned that high rates of sexual diseases in Australia's Aboriginal community offered ideal ground for an explosion in the numbers of those infected with the Human Immunodeficiency Virus, which can lead to Aquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.
"While the diagnosed rates of HIV infection remains low (in Aboriginal communities), there is huge potential for the spread of HIV under such circumstances," said Puplick.
There are an estimated 300,000 Aborigines in Australia 18 million population.
